title: Establish compact ledger markers for hedged, speculative, and replayed streaming requests
creator: Evan Miller
description:
Background:
Customers have observed incorrect token tallies when our gateway issues hedged requests, when clients perform speculative replays, or when intermittent network reconnects produce overlapping fragments. Existing ledger entries are fine-grained (per-fragment) which simplifies attribution but explodes state and makes dedup across replays expensive. This ticket proposes a compact ledger-marker design: a lightweight anchor placed at strategic checkpoints (start-of-request, periodic anchors, terminal anchors) that enables deterministic deduplication and correct token accounting across hedged/speculative/replayed flows while bounding memory and I/O costs.

Problem statement (symptoms and failure modes):
- Duplicate token debits when hedged requests both complete and the system credits both outputs.
- Orphaned provisional credits for speculative partials followed by a later definitive output from a different backend.
- Large per-fragment ledger growth for long-lived streams and attachment-heavy flows.
- High reconciliation latency during tenant audits because all fragments must be examined for replay detection.

Proposed solution (overview):
1) Introduce compact ledger markers (CLMs): short fixed-format markers with the following fields encoded in the marker payload string: request-origin-id, stream-seq-range (start..end or open), backend-instance-hash (optional), marker-type (anchor/checkpoint/terminal), and a marker-version tag. Markers are written atomically alongside existing fragment credits.
2) Dedup semantics: when processing a fragment or terminal event, the reconciler consults the nearest CLM for that stream. If the fragment's offset falls within an already-finalized seq-range anchored by a terminal marker, the fragment is treated as a replay and not double-counted.
3) Hedged request handling: hedged requests will emit shared origin-ids. The first terminal marker observed finalizes the seq-range; subsequent completions carrying the same origin-id or overlapping seq-range are deduped.
4) Compaction policy: periodic background compaction replaces multi-fragment chains with a single synthesized CLM representing the consolidated seq-range and a final token tally snapshot. Compaction is tenant-aware and bounded by per-tenant retention config.
5) Migration: write CLMs in parallel with current per-fragment ledger entries for 2 weeks, enable reconciler to prefer CLMs, then run one-time compaction job to reduce historic state.

Design trade-offs and rationale:
- Why markers vs global dedupe table: CLMs are append-only and colocated with stream state which avoids global coordination for every fragment, reducing latency and contention.
- Memory vs IO: markers add small write overhead but allow dramatic compaction later; we target <1% increase in per-fragment write bytes before compaction.
- Determinism: marker-version ensures forward compatibility; reconciler falls back to fragment-scan if marker version mismatch detected.

Operational concerns:
- Metrics to add: marker-write-rate, marker-compaction-rate, dedupe-hit-rate, stale-marker-age distribution, reconciliation-time-per-tenant.
- Failure modes: partial compaction runs; reconciler must be idempotent and possess safe fallbacks to re-scan fragments.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 1: implement CLM write path in gateway and runtime; add marker schema and wire format. (PR: draft linked in comments)
- Phase 2: extend reconciler to consult CLMs, implement hedged-origin-id matching logic, add unit/integration tests.
- Phase 3: roll write-only toggled via feature flag; run canary on internal tenants.
- Phase 4: enable CLM-first reconciliation, start compaction job, monitor metrics and audits.

Rollout constraints and feature flags:
- Feature flag: metering.clm.write (write-only); metering.clm.reconcile (read/reconcile path); metering.clm.compact (compaction job).
- Default: all flags off. Progressive enablement: internal tenants -> alpha customers -> all.

Notes on compatibility with streaming replay/resume protocol:
- CLMs include the resume-offset semantics that map 1:1 with existing resume tokens so clients see no change. The reconciler must map fragment offsets to CLM seq-ranges deterministically.

Open design questions (to resolve during implementation):
- Exact max encoded size for CLM to guarantee in-line storage within existing ledger records.
- TTL/retention policy per-customer and compaction intervals.
- Schema for marker-version evolution and migration strategy for older runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No duplicate token debits in hedged request test harness across 10k hedged pairs; 2) Compaction reduces historic ledger size by >=40% on sample tenant; 3) Dedup hit-rate >95% for synthetic speculative replay workloads; 4) Reconciler falls back safely and produces identical audit reports to pre-CLM baseline within noise tolerances; 5) Feature flags allow safe rollback without data loss.
test_plan: Unit tests for CLM encode/decode and boundary seq-range checks; integration simulation harness that spawns hedged pairs, network reconnects, and speculative replays and validates final token tallies against an oracle; end-to-end canary on three internal tenants for 48 hours with metrics collection; run audit diff job comparing reconciler outputs before and after CLM reconciliation on a 7-day historic window; fault-injection tests for partial compaction and marker-version mismatch.

2026-03-07 - Priya Raghavan: Implementation started. Schema proto added to runtime repo. WIP PR: see attachments.
2026-03-09 - QA: added integration harness tasks to cycle. Need deterministic oracle for token counts; using existing tokenization library to ensure parity.
2026-03-12 - Code review: PR left comments about idempotent writes and retry window. Priya to address dedupe of duplicate marker writes on transient flaps.
Follow-ups: schedule on-call walkthrough for compaction failures; add runbook entry for forced rollback that toggles metering.clm.reconcile=false and re-runs legacy reconciliation if needed.
